title: Durable project orchestration with parallel workers and serial delivery
outcomes: Run two independent task builds concurrently while preserving individual task lifecycle and release evidence.
Recover project coordination without duplicate workers, unknown publication retries or chat-dependent state.

in: Single-host project scheduler, admission, bounded native workers, durable phase-boundary messages, integration reconciliation and serial publication
out: Implementation or execution in this design turn
Cross-host coordination, live session injection, nested agent teams, new provider adapters and GitHub Actions
boundaries: One canonical .go control state; distinct task worktrees; serialized integration/release channel

concerns: A verified release per release-required task
decision_rights: Authorize implementation, task models, run budget and publication destinations

concerns: No stale evidence or hidden authority expansion
decision_rights: Schedule within frozen authority and validated task/resource contracts; implementation not yet authorized

constraints: Proposed design only; existing single-task runtime rules remain authoritative until changed and verified.
Retain existing task/run/workspace/completion records; project state references them rather than duplicating completion truth.
Use explicit parallel opt-in, two builders initially, native CLI workers and one host.
Distinguish worker paths from controller-only release paths without exceeding total task scope.
Use history-preserving base reconciliation, scope attribution and renewed final verification/critic before release.
No worker chat message grants authority or satisfies a completion/dependency gate.
2026-09-19 priority change: parallel implementation deferred to after verified serial autonomy; see .go/plans/autonomy-first.json. This draft is not an active implementation prerequisite.

quality_attributes.scenario: Two independent eligible tasks with explicit parallel opt-in
Controller crash, duplicate dispatch or surviving orphan
quality_attributes.measure: Concurrent writers for the same task/workspace generation

quality_attributes.scenario: Task A releases while B is still building
quality_attributes.measure: B releases using evidence from before base reconciliation
Active publisher reservations on one release channel

quality_attributes.scenario: Worker message, model switch request or capacity increase
quality_attributes.measure: Unapproved expansion of frozen task/run authority

risks: Worktree isolation does not isolate databases, ports, generated files or hostile subprocesses.
The integration/release lane may dominate runtime; more workers can increase stale work rather than throughput.
Merge reconciliation requires task-specific attribution; inherited upstream changes cannot simply be checked against the original base.
open_questions: Before live proof: select an authorized pilot project, model profiles, budget and publication destination.
O1 must freeze exact versioned fields and CLI/API boundaries; illustrative design states are not an implemented schema.
